verses.text: The two angels reached Sodom in the evening. Lot was sitting at the city gate. When he saw them, he stood up, went to meet them, and bowed with his face to the ground.
He said, "My lords, please come to your servant's home. Stay the night, wash your feet, then get up early and continue your journey." They said, "No, we'll spend the night in the open square."
But Lot kept urging them, so they went home with him. He prepared a feast, baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
Before they went to bed, the men of Sodom surrounded the house. Young and old, people from every part of the city, were there.
They shouted to Lot, "Where are the men who came to your house tonight? Bring them out so we can rape them."
Lot went outside to meet them and shut the door behind him.
He said, "Please, my brothers, don't do this wicked thing.
Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them out to you, and you can do what you think is right. But don't harm these men; they came under the protection of my roof."

They said, "Get out of our way!" Then they said, "This foreigner came here to live, and now he wants to judge us. We'll treat you worse than them!" They shoved Lot hard and moved in to break down the door.
But the men inside reached out, pulled Lot back into the house, and shut the door.
Then they struck the men outside with blindness, both young and old. The men wore themselves out trying to find the doorway.
The men asked Lot, "Do you have anyone else here—sons-in-law, sons, daughters, or anyone in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of this place.
We're going to destroy this place. The outcry against its people has become great before Yahweh, and Yahweh sent us to destroy it."
Lot went out and spoke to the men pledged to marry his daughters. "Get up! Leave this place, because Yahweh is going to destroy the city!" But they thought he was joking.
At dawn, the angels urged Lot: "Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you'll be swept away in the city's punishment."
Lot hesitated. But Yahweh had mercy on him, so the men took his hand, his wife's hand, and the hands of his two daughters. They led them out and left them beyond the city.
Once they had brought them outside, one said, "Run for your life! Don't look back or stop anywhere in the plain. Escape to the hills, or you'll be swept away."
Lot said to them, "Please, my lord, don't make me do that.
You have shown your servant favor and great kindness by saving my life. But I can't escape to the hills; disaster might catch up with me, and I'll die.
Look, there's a small city close enough to reach. Please let me escape there—it's only a little place—and my life will be spared."
He answered, "All right. I'll grant this request too. I won't overthrow the city you're talking about.
Hurry and get there, because I can't act until you arrive." That's why the city was named Zoar.
The sun had risen over the land by the time Lot reached Zoar.
Then Yahweh sent burning sulfur and fire down on Sodom and Gomorrah from Yahweh in the sky.
He overthrew those cities, the whole plain, everyone living in the cities, and everything growing from the ground.
But Lot's wife looked back behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
Abraham got up early and went to the place where he had stood before Yahweh.
He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and across the whole plain. He saw smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace.
When God destroyed the cities of the plain, he remembered Abraham and brought Lot out of the destruction that swallowed the cities where Lot had lived.
Lot was afraid to stay in Zoar, so he went up into the hills with his two daughters. They lived in a cave.
The older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there's no man on earth to have a family with us the way people everywhere do.
Let's get our father drunk with wine, then sleep with him so our father's family line can continue."
That night they gave their father wine to drink. The older daughter went in and slept with him. He didn't know when she lay down or when she got up.

The next day, the older daughter told the younger, "I slept with our father last night. Let's get him drunk with wine again tonight, and you go in and sleep with him. Then our father's family line can continue."
That night they gave their father wine to drink again. The younger daughter went and slept with him. He didn't know when she lay down or when she got up.
So both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older daughter gave birth to a son and named him Moab. He became the ancestor of the Moabites who live today.
The younger daughter also gave birth to a son and named him Ben-ammi. He became the ancestor of the Ammonites who live today.
